subject: Pilot pricing: floor cap and streaming rounding clarification
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthscope.ai>

Cc: procurement@healthscope.ai, elena.ruiz@healthscope.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pilot billing: streaming + long history

Hi Neha / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — HealthScope is excited to pilot Redwood for our clinical summarization pipeline. Before we move SOW/PO, procurement has a couple of technical billing asks we need clarified so finance can sign off: 

1) Pilot cap: our CFO wants a clear monthly ceiling for the pilot (expected 30k generated tokens peak across jobs). Can you confirm if you can put a hard cap or an automatic stop once X spend is reached?

2) Rounding for streaming: our model sends streaming responses that sometimes produce very short tails (<40 tokens). How are those billed — do you round up to your metering quantum? We need examples for 1–10 token tails and 200+ token bursts.

3) Context reuse credits: we will reuse patient conversation prefixes a lot (same prompt history across calls). Is there a prefix/kv-cache credit we can rely on during pilot? Any sample invoice line showing credits would help.

4) Minimums vs true-up: if we commit to a 3-month pilot, can you cap minimums (we'd like to avoid a large minimum on month 1) and true-up at the end of the pilot?

Attached is our usage projection workbook and a draft SOW. Can someone from pricing share the exact rounding math and a sample pilot invoice row?

Best,
Samir
Head of Engineering
HealthScope AI

Attachments: HealthScope_MVP_usage_projection.xlsx (xlsx), HS-Pilot_SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pilot billing: streaming + long history

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Looping Karthik (pricing) and Marissa for pilot commercial guardrails. Answers at a high level below; Karthik I'll let you drop the math and sample invoice rows.

1) Pilot cap / spend stop: we can implement a hard spend cap for the pilot and an automatic stop when reached. Typical process: we set a soft alert at 80% and stop at the configured cap. Can do per-project cap (sits on your account) or per-route caps if you want to isolate ingestion jobs.

2) Streaming rounding: our metering quantum is 50 token units for streaming payloads by default. That means any tail <=50 tokens in a single streaming fragment is billed as 50 tokens. For larger bursts we bucket into 50-token increments (e.g., 201 tokens -> 5 quanta = 250 tokens billed). Karthik — please add any exceptions (e.g., behavior when a fragment is an immediate retry or blank).

3) Context/reuse credit: for pilot customers we offer a prefix reuse credit model: repeated prefixes that match at the same route and model receive an incremental KV-cache credit (not a flat token refund) — effectively reducing billable tokens for repeated identical prefixes. We can map this to an invoice line as “KV cache credit — prefix reuse”. For pilot terms we can pilot a 60% effective credit on repeated prefix tokens up to a configured prefix length (we'll show math).

4) Minimums and true-up: we can offer a dampened minimum for the first month (cap the minimum at $4k) and true-up at the end of the 3-month pilot with a single invoice reconciliation. Alternatively, we can waive month-1 minimum and require a 3-month aggregate minimum.

Action items: Karthik to provide detailed rounding examples + sample invoice entries; Marissa to confirm commercial concession language (pilot minimum / true-up); Vanessa to coordinate PO/SOW language with procurement.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi all — dumping the worked examples below so procurement has concrete rows for PO approval. I've included sample invoice lines and a short table of cases.

Metering assumptions (pilot config): model: rw-large-2026, metering quantum: 50 tokens; prefix credit: 60% effective credit on identical prefix tokens up to 1024-token prefix; pilot monthly cap allowed: enabled; true-up: monthly invoice plus a single aggregate reconciliation at pilot end.

Examples (billable tokens):
- Single-stream tail (8 tokens): billed = 50 tokens -> cost = 50 * unit_price
- Small burst (47 tokens): billed = 50 tokens
- Medium burst (210 tokens): billed = 250 tokens (5 quanta)
- Large burst (3,412 tokens): billed = 3,450 tokens (69 quanta)

Prefix reuse credit (worked):
- Call A prefix: 512 tokens repeated 100x across month = raw prefix tokens = 51,200 tokens. Effective credit = 60% -> credited amount = 30,720 tokens removed from billable. Remaining billable tokens dependent on per-call unique suffix.

Sample invoice rows (illustrative numbers only):
1) rw-large-2026 token consumption (gross): 1,200,000 tokens -> $0.0008 per token -> line = $960.00
2) Prefix reuse credit (kv-cache): -30,720 tokens -> credit line = -$24.576 -> shown as separate negative invoice line
3) Pilot minimum (month 1) floor applied: $4,000 (if actual bill < floor, invoice shows floor less credits)
4) Monthly cap trigger: if cap = $6,000 and usage hits cap, system halts ingestion and we send alert at 80%

Notes / caveats:
- Streaming fragments from retries can be deduplicated server-side if request idempotency is enabled, which avoids double-billing of transient fragments. We'll need HealthScope to use a per-call idempotency token for long-running jobs.
- If you enable long-term cache pinning (reserved KV for the pilot) there is an operational fee; we can discuss if that's necessary.

Happy to refine the sample invoice to match your projected numbers — I used conservative unit prices for illustration.

-Karthik
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference
